gap-w6-039.question: Does the pass@1 versus pass@64 reversal appear in our ledger?
gap-w6-039.reading: A flip is the same campaign, same task, same verifier, both a 1 and a 0 in different rounds. That is the reversal in binary form: the score of one attempt is not a property of the task. pass@1 counts round 1 only and therefore understates what k rounds reach; the gap between passAt1 and passAtK is the reversal, and it is also why src/runtime/selector.js preferring unsolved tasks is worse than it looks -- "unsolved" is often "unlucky".

gap-w6-011.question: How many verifications were executed rather than asserted?

beforeVerifierLoggingExists.note: verifier.finished did not exist yet; absence here is a logging fact, not a measurement of the work.

gap-w6-011.reading: The first version of this measurement pooled the eras and reported 75 attempts with a gate verdict and no verifier event, passing at 56.7% against 42.1% for the measured ones -- which would have meant unverified work succeeds more often. It does not. Zero of those 210 attempts before the era line could have had a verifier event (nothing wrote them), and after the line only 5 attempts reached a gate without one, none scoring. The pooled "executed rate" of 0.559 is therefore a fact about when the event was added to the log, not about how often we verify; the honest number is 0.792 for the era that can answer. This is exp-gap-004 a second time in one night: a quantity computed over two populations reported as one.

gap-w6-001.question: What is the actual human decision rate in dsh-loom?
gap-w6-001.reading: The rate that matters for cost is decisions per campaign, not per attempt: a campaign needing zero decisions is the unattended case the design targets. Answer rate is not decision quality -- an answered checkpoint includes "rejected because stale", which is a bookkeeping outcome, not a judgement about the work.

gap-w6-018.question: Is a single-run SEM of 0.8-1.4 points enough to justify the 1-3 point deltas the ledger promotes?
gap-w6-018.reading: The premise of the question is a units error. A SEM in "points" belongs to a benchmark whose score is a share of many tasks; our score is one binary verdict on one task, so its noise is Bernoulli, not 0.8-1.4 points. At the pooled rate that is sqrt(p(1-p)) per candidate and sqrt(2) times that for a difference of two candidates -- both printed above. The consequence for minGain is that any threshold below that difference-SD is a coin flip dressed as a decision, which is what exp-gate-001 measured from the other end (0 of 208 gate decisions had a real incumbent to compare against).
